structured.approach:
I followed the frontend-steps FE-04 procedure and read the contracted inputs: task.components, feat.design, feat.stories, feat.screens, org.design_library, org.engineering_stack and org.lessons. I read every repository file I cite with the Read tool: src/ap_portal/index.js, CLAUDE.md, package.json, ci.mjs, README.md and docs/ap_portal.md.

In src/ap_portal/index.js I implemented task.components section 3.1 items 1.1 to 1.9, following the feat.design B4.2 algorithm and the feat.screens FS-1/FS-2 markup. Every change is additive, and each new constant and function has a `//` comment. I documented the module in docs/ap_portal.md and README.md.

I ran `node ci.mjs` and `git status`. In the claims I describe the CI outcome in words and use only the threshold number that appears in ci.mjs.

CI measures coverage only from tests/*.test.js, and tests/ is outside this step's write scope. Coverage therefore stays below the threshold until FE-05 adds the tests that task.code lists; this is raised as an open question. No connectors or secrets were used, and nothing was committed.
tools_used: Bash (node ci.mjs, git status, git diff)

claims.text: renderOverdueRisk was added to src/ap_portal/index.js and exported, together with the private helpers escapeHtml, toTwoDecimalString and riskClass and the constants RISK_CLASSES, OVERDUE_HEADINGS, HTML_ESCAPES and DECIMAL_STRING, placed where the design puts them.
Every new constant and every new function in src/ap_portal/index.js has a // comment directly above it.

renderOverdueRisk returns '' for undefined, null or an empty array. It throws TypeError when rows is not an array or when a days value is not an integer. Otherwise it renders <table class="overdue-risk">, a header row with no class (Invoice, Vendor, Days overdue, Amount), then one tr with class risk-<risk> per row in the order given.
Amounts are displayed with string operations only: a decimal-string regex check, then padEnd to two decimals. Number(), parseFloat and formatAmount are never used, in line with D-2026-044 and L-011.
id and vendor are HTML-escaped (&, <, >, ", '). The row class comes from an allow-list, so an unknown risk value renders risk-unknown.
LABELS, formatAmount and renderAgingSummary are unchanged, which follows the rule to keep existing public signatures and add new functions for new behaviour.
VERSION in src/ap_portal/index.js moved from 2.3.0 to 2.4.0. package.json still says 2.3.0 because it is outside this step's write scope.

node ci.mjs reports that the sources compile, both existing tests pass and there are no static issues. CI fails only because line coverage is below its coverage >= 90 threshold: no test calls the new function bodies yet.
CI measures coverage from tests/*.test.js and requires coverage >= 90, but this step may change only src/ap_portal/, docs/ and README.md.

docs/ap_portal.md was added. It covers the module overview, exports, signature, CT-1 inputs, outputs, TypeError cases, examples and private helpers. README.md now lists renderOverdueRisk and links to the docs.

open_questions: CQ-FE-5: CI line coverage is below the 90% threshold after FE-04, because tests/ is outside this step's write scope. FE-05 must add the tests listed in task.code section 5 before FE-06 commits and pushes.
CQ-FE-4: package.json "version" (2.3.0) must move together with VERSION (2.4.0), but package.json is outside FE-04's write scope. Should FE-05 or FE-06 update it, or should the spine widen the scope?
CQ-FE-3: The Developer needs to confirm the version number 2.4.0.

Carried, non-blocking: CQ-FE-1 (who styles the risk-* classes), CQ-FE-2 (no approved Figma frames), RA-1 (branch name feature/story), and TQ-7, TQ-11, OQ-B8, TQ-6, OQ-B9, PQ-P7 and DQ-3, which are implemented on their interim designs.
structured.summary:
CI still fails for STORY-07 on ap_portal: line coverage is below the 90% threshold. The new code has no tests yet because this step cannot change tests/. FE-05 has to add them, and task.code.md lists exactly which ones. The rest of CI passes: the code compiles, both existing tests pass and there are no static issues.

The code is in src/ap_portal/index.js: renderOverdueRisk plus three commented private helpers, built to feat.design B4 and the feat.screens FS-1/FS-2 markup. Amounts are handled as strings only. id and vendor are HTML-escaped, the risk class comes from an allow-list, and no rows gives an empty string. The existing functions are unchanged.

VERSION is now 2.4.0, but package.json still says 2.3.0 because it is outside this step's scope. I added docs/ap_portal.md and updated README.md. Nothing was committed.
